title: SEC1: Asymmetric DKIM signing failure handling (NNTP defer vs SMTP dead-letter)
description:
Maintainer Burden — Error Path Consistency

The two queues implement opposite semantics for DKIM signing failure:
  • queue.rs:217–234 (NNTP): Signs inside drain loop; defers on error; retries next cycle
  • relay_queue.rs:340–368 (SMTP relay): Signs before relay; moves to dead-letter on error

Current behavior:
  • NNTP articles stuck in queue retry indefinitely (potential silent loss of service if signing is permanently broken)
  • SMTP relay articles move to dead-letter immediately (immediate mail loss)

Risk: Solo maintainer will struggle to remember which path uses which strategy. If a DKIM signing bug is discovered, one path will hide data loss and the other will lose mail immediately.

Recommendation: Align error handling semantics OR add explicit comments explaining why they differ. Consider: should DKIM signing failure be treated as transient (retry) or permanent (dead-letter)?
